# Port a representative slice of the pinned public repo to Phrase
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #126, sha256:f8ff9dc876869d0ac74d4b48f5383f831e0a82cc56caa4abde6aafa487527c4c). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; a private port)
- **Milestone:** Codebase size: does Phrase's cost fall and its edge widen as the codebase grows?
- **Source:** Steve's answers relayed by Dispatch, 2026-10-27 (use a publicly available repository instead of his private projects, and optionally a growth study) and Decider D84 (Codex Yes; Grok Support-it; Copilot out of quota). Separate from the frozen bar (D32); nothing is re-scored. The private projects play-tracker and BaccaratSim are dropped and are never snapshotted, opened or referenced.
- **Depends on:** 125
- **Story:** As Ari, I want a representative slice of the pinned public repository written in Phrase beside its C# original, so that modify and fix tasks on real code can be given in both languages.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given the pinned slice (one module or bounded context), When the mob writes the Phrase version, Then it compiles with the C# adapter and its generated specs pass the same outcome cases as the original's tests (outcome parity), with native csharp blocks only where Phrase has no vocabulary, counted and reported as a total
  2. Given the two versions, When modify and fix tasks are written, Then each needs context from another file of the slice and the tasks are pre-registered before any run (new tasks are written for this experiment, not taken from the repository's issues)
  3. Given the port, When the repository checks run, Then the port and the fetched copy are untracked and attribution to the original licence is kept in the private folder

## Context

- PUBLIC-REPO RULES (D84): the pinned source is fetched into a git-ignored folder and never committed; only a pin file (URL, SPDX licence, exact commit SHA, tree hash, slice paths, endpoint counts of the repo and the slice, toolchain and dependency versions) is tracked; the original licence and attribution are kept with the private copy; the commit must build and its tests pass at pin time, with endpoints counted by a rule declared before counting; contamination risk is recorded per repo as a caveat (a famous C# repository probably favours the plain C# arm); rows go to private results and only totals are published.
